preconditions.description: The number of test cases T is between 1 and 5 inclusive.
For each test case, the number of cities N is between 2 and 5000 inclusive.
For each test case, the number of external road proposals M1 is between 1 and 20000 inclusive.
For each test case, the number of Chef's road proposals M2 is between 1 and 20000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= c <= 1000000000 for c in all_costs)
preconditions.description: For every proposed road, the cost c is between 0 and 1,000,000,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(u != v for u, v in all_road_endpoints)
preconditions.description: For every proposed road, the two endpoints u and v are distinct cities.

postconditions.description: If a valid spanning tree exists, the output contains non-negative integers for maximum profit and minimum total cost; otherwise, it indicates impossibility.
The output is 'Impossible' if and only if the union of all proposed roads cannot connect all N cities into a single component.

postconditions.expression: not is_impossible and max_profit == max(profit(S) for S in all_spanning_trees(N, external_roads, chef_roads))
postconditions.description: If possible, max_profit is the maximum sum of costs of Chef's roads among all valid spanning trees.

postconditions.expression: not is_impossible and min_total_cost == min(total_cost(S) for S in all_spanning_trees(N, external_roads, chef_roads) if profit(S) == max_profit)
postconditions.description: If possible, min_total_cost is the minimum sum of costs of all roads (Chef's and external) among all spanning trees that achieve the maximum profit.
If no spanning tree exists, the output is exactly the string 'Impossible'.
If a spanning tree exists, the output is two space-separated integers: the maximum profit and the corresponding minimum total cost.
